function: Diffusion model generates power-splitting factors and power-control coefficients that maximize downlink sum spectral efficiency of rate-splitting cell-free massive MIMO (pp. 7-9)
system: Cell-free massive MIMO, L=20 APs with N=4 antennas, K=4 single-antenna UEs, no RIS; 2 GHz carrier, 20 MHz bandwidth, 500 m x 500 m area (pp. 3, 10)
method: Conditional diffusion model (noise-prediction network, T=10 denoising steps) trained by supervised imitation of genetic-algorithm expert solutions with a denoising loss (pp. 8-9)
data_channel: Own simulation: spatially correlated Rician channel, three-slope path loss; Rician factor -10 to 20 dB and ASD 5-90 deg grids; genetic-algorithm expert labels (pp. 3, 9)
test_conditions: Trained and tested under identical conditions and datasets (p. 12); Fig. 9 tests Rician factor -10 to 10 dB and ASD 10-90 deg, inside the training grid (pp. 9, 12)
baselines: Without RS; equal and heuristic power-splitting and power-control; genetic algorithm as expert upper bound; learned DRL with PPO [30] (pp. 11-12)
metrics: Sum spectral efficiency (CDF, versus transmit power, number of APs, Rician factor, ASD, initial power-splitting factor and training epoch) (pp. 10-12)
complexity: Order O(Ngai(G+T wa+wc)) versus O(Ndrl(G+wa+wc)) for DRL, in terms of iterations, denoising steps and network weights; no FLOPs or runtime values (p. 9)
q1_support: p. 9: "Utilizing the three-slope propagation model [1], [19]," Own simulator: spatially correlated Rician channel with LoS and NLoS terms defined on p. 3 ("is modeled as Rician") and three-slope path loss; no 3GPP TR 38.901, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 12: "trained and tested under identical conditions, datasets" Fig. 9 (p. 12) tests Rician factors -10 to 10 dB and ASD 10-90 deg, inside the training grid of p. 9 (-10 to 20 dB, 5-90 deg); no unseen scenario, number of APs, UEs or antennas, or fine-tuning is reported for the GAI model.
q3_support: p. 12: "DRL-based algorithm that uses Proximal Policy Optimization" is the learned baseline, compared on sum SE in Fig. 8; p. 12: "exceeds twice that of the heuristic algorithm" is the non-learned comparison on sum SE in Fig. 9.
q4_support: p. 9: "algorithm can be expressed as O(Ngai (G+T wa +wc )), where" gives the order of complexity of the proposed method; it is symbolic and no measured runtime or FLOPs are reported.
q5_support: p. 9: "We compute a small number of expert solutions for training and" inference: the data are self-generated by simulation; the paper gives no code or data link and uses no public channel dataset.
notes: Borderline area: the learned output is power allocation (power-splitting factors rho_l and power-control coefficients eta_il) that scales fixed MR and superposition-based precoders at each AP (p. 4, Eq. 14), classed as area 3 (base station precoder); if power control alone is not precoder design, exclude as function. Journal paper whose main contribution is a closed-form sum-SE analysis (p. 2); the learned part is Section IV. The expert solutions for training come from a genetic algorithm (p. 9).
